column6: Both describe the same attack: user or external content alters LLM behavior (direct/indirect prompt injection).
OWASP LLM01 explicitly treats jailbreaking as a form of prompt injection; ATLAS models it as its own technique.
Sensitive information disclosure through model outputs is ATLAS's LLM Data Leakage technique.
LLM supply-chain risk (models, data, plugins, platforms) corresponds to ATLAS AI Supply Chain Compromise.
Data and model poisoning during pre-training/fine-tuning/embedding is ATLAS's Poison Training Data technique.
Vector/embedding weaknesses in RAG systems are exploited by ATLAS's RAG Poisoning technique.
System prompt leakage corresponds to ATLAS's Extract LLM System Prompt technique.
OWASP's Excessive Agency preventions (require human approval for high-impact actions) correspond to ATLAS's Human In-the-Loop for AI Agent Actions mitigation.
Unbounded consumption includes denial-of-service against the model — ATLAS Denial of AI Service.
Unbounded consumption includes unsustainable inference costs — ATLAS Cost Harvesting.

Article 15(5) requires high-risk systems to be resilient against attacks that 'manipulate the training data set (data poisoning)' and 'pre-trained components (model poisoning)' — the attacks this technique performs.
